CLOSES THE ONLY KNOWN DEFECT SHIPPED BY THIS PROJECT - epic-03-learnings section 7a. The TEMPO Y axis was labelled 'min' while carrying seconds since ticket-025, and the suite POSITIVELY asserted that no division had happened, checking the PL figure exceeded 60. It asserted both halves of a contradiction, and no guardian caught it because each half was individually correct. Measured closure, reproduced independently by the guardian from the fixture and the shipped settings.json: PL was 4492.11 raw seconds for the etapa alone; the PL GROUP sums 4492.11 + the two other etapas to 8905.16 seconds, and round(8905.16 / 60.0, 2) = 148.42 minutes is what the payload now carries. unit_divisor appears in exactly two modules, config.py and dashboard/scalars.py, so the division happens once. No test anywhere still pins a second-valued TEMPO at the payload or document layer; the raw-second references in test_consolidate.py, test_fixtures_sintese.py and test_readers.py are below scalars.py, where ticket-018 deliberately keeps seconds.

THE LENIENT-GROUP / STRICT-TOTAL ASYMMETRY, verified the ticket-030 way - by building both wrong implementations and measuring. Making TOTAL lenient produced 15.0 where the correct answer is to omit the cell: a silently wrong, too-low total. Making a group strict produced None where the correct value is 10.0: a needlessly dropped bar. The asymmetry is right because a group's member etapas are internal to one bar, so a partial sum costs that bar precision, while the groups are separately displayed bars, so a partial TOTAL reports a number that is simply wrong.

A SPECIALIST FINDING ITS OWN TEST WRONG, worth carrying forward as the standard: its first -0.0 test was arithmetically impossible, and rather than adjust the code it traced WHY - TOTAL sums already-normalised group values, and IEEE 754 addition of a value and its exact negation yields +0.0, so -0.0 is reachable only at the group conversion step. It then retargeted the test at the path that can actually produce it.

BYTE-FOR-BYTE REPRODUCIBILITY was broken and no test could see it. scalars.py iterated a set[tuple[str, str]] to insert the scenario/deck keys of every aggregated scalar series, so insertion order followed the per-process randomised string hash and the same inputs produced byte-different HTML. Invisible to the suite because the only repeatability test compares two builds INSIDE ONE PROCESS. Verified by running under PYTHONHASHSEED - and the first attempt nearly refuted it, since three seeds agreed by chance; confirming the seed was propagating and widening the sample showed seed 777 reversing even the outer key order. Fixed with sorted() at three sites; 601/601 then passed under PYTHONHASHSEED=777, proving nothing depended on the arbitrary order.

A CONFIGURABLE DIVISOR UNDER A HARD-CODED LABEL (finding 3): time.unit_divisor is a documented tunable validated only as positive, while FALLBACK_UNITS['TEMPO'] is the constant 'min'. Setting unit_divisor to 1.0 would re-introduce the exact defect ticket-031 had just closed, with every test green, because the tests pinned the two halves separately and never together. Fixed with a Portuguese warning plus one test that asserts label and divisor AS A PAIR. General rule: where a label and a value are separately configurable, a test must assert their correspondence, not each half.

THE SIMPLIFIER'S MOST VALUABLE OUTPUT WAS NOT A SIMPLIFICATION. It correctly filed the reproducibility defect in its own section as 'not a simplification - please rule on this one' rather than burying it among refactors. It also predicted that its single applied edit might trip ruff's isort rule, which it did.

MEASURING BEAT ESTIMATING TWICE MORE AT THIS BOUNDARY. The simplifier estimated the live defect-20 docstring residue at five modules; measurement found ELEVEN, spanning epic 3 as well as epic 4. And the correct fix was the one it argued for: fix the DOCSTRING, not the value, because changing stage_groups would move the TEMPO bar count and the measured byte range in test_output_size.py.

refinement_inputs: ORDERING RISK CHECKED AND ABSENT, 2026-09-11. The parity check therefore still has its reference implementation in the working tree when it runs. Do not reorder these two under any circumstances.

TICKET-035 INHERITS THE COST-CHART PARITY TENSION recorded in ticket-030's Context. Plotadores/Custos.py emits THREE separate cost figures with the Y-axis titles 'Custo Presente (R$)', 'Custo Futuro (R$)' and 'Custo Total de Operacao (R$)'. Refine ticket-035 to compare presentation as well as values.

TICKET-038 OPEN QUESTION ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-11: no __pycache__ path is tracked any more (git ls-files finds none) and .gitignore line 2 covers __pycache__/, so ticket-001 already handled it. The cost-chart presentation decision above is unresolved and its only evidence is Plotadores/Custos.py. HARD CONSTRAINT, NEVER REORDER: ticket-035 before ticket-038. 038 deletes Plotadores/, which is 035's reference implementation, and 038 requirement 2 additionally makes 035's parity report a precondition it verifies before deleting anything. AMENDED 2026-09-11 after the epic-04 boundary landed mid-refinement. shipped_code_defects_found_by_refinement: THE INSTRUCTION TO REFINE AGAINST THE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN THE PLAN PAID FOR ITSELF: eleven defects in shipped code, none of which any per-ticket guardian could have caught. DEAD FLAG, orchestrator-verified: --modo-inicial is declared in cli.build_parser (cli.py:75) and recorded in the manifest params (cli.py:144), and pipeline.py contains ZERO references to it. write_dashboard defaults initial_mode to 'encadeado'. So a user passing --modo-inicial por-deck gets a chained dashboard AND a manifest asserting the mode they asked for. That is worse than a no-op: the audit record lies. Section 5's shape again - the parser half and the pipeline half each correct alone, no ticket owning the correspondence. DEGRADATION RECORDS NEVER REACH THE LOG, orchestrator-verified: DashboardData.add_warning (store.py:278-281) only appends to a list. Every degradation - a missing deck, a missing file, a dropped submarket - reaches the HTML Avisos section and NOTHING ELSE. No console line, no rotating log file entry. Owned by ticket-033 (manifest plus count) and ticket-037 (per-message, capped at 20).

CHECKLIST SECTION 9 IS GUARDED BY NO TEST. Only two test modules reference the checklist at all, and test_charts_times.py is not one of them - so step 30's min-not-seconds check and step 29's read-and-record measurement could be deleted by a simplifier without breaking anything. Resolved 2026-09-10: the 240 exemplo worktree deletions are intentional. ticket-001 stages them via git rm -r --cached (index only); the developer commits them with .gitignore.

Resolved 2026-09-10: example tree rebuilt from git HEAD into exemplo/caso_oficial and exemplo/caso_gurobi (2 decks each, gitignored). ticket-034 defaults to it, DESSEM_DASHBOARD_EXEMPLO overrides, skip when absent.

Resolved 2026-09-10 by the developer (epic-03 decision E3-1): the renderer is tested with Python-only assertions on the generated HTML and JSON plus a manual checklist under docs/. No JS engine and no Node toolchain (measured: node and npm are absent from this WSL environment). Accepted trade-off: the browser-side difference computation of master plan decision 8 has no automated test, mitigated by keeping the JS thin and naming the case in the checklist.

Resolved 2026-09-10 by the developer (epic-03 decision E3-2): the chart heading is always the curated ChartSpec.title; Registries.title_for supplies an additive subtitle or hover text where it differs. Measured against the real METADADOS_OPERACAO: the registry name is better where the curated title is an acronym (CMO, EARMF) but would collapse the hm3-versus-percent and afluente-versus-incremental distinctions that resolved master plan open questions 2 and 3.

Resolved 2026-09-10 by orchestrator ruling: URL-hash state shared by the deck selector and the level navigation is OUT OF SCOPE. The spec does not require linkable views, so refinement must not introduce hash routing. Reopen only on an explicit developer request.

Resolved 2026-09-11 (epic-04 decision E4-3): the plant payload stays FULLY EMBEDDED, because the deliverable is one self-contained offline HTML and any lazy fetch needs a server or sibling files. Size is managed by rounding to output.decimals, omitting entities whose arrays are entirely null, and ticket-032 measuring and warning. Lazy RENDERING already exists: ticket-023 renders only the active group. Refine 032 together with 027. Measured motivation: the epic-03 payload alone reaches about 56 MB at 30 decks times 3 scenarios, past the 50 MB default.

Resolved 2026-09-11 (epic-04 decision E4-4): filtering plants by submarket and by equivalent reservoir is OUT OF SCOPE. The spec asks for name and code filters only; the registry supports more, which is why it is tempting, but it is unrequested scope. Consistent with the epic-03 ruling on URL-hash state. Reopen only on explicit request.
